description: Two-panel composite of calculated equilibrium phase-proportion diagrams sharing identical axes: y = Phase percentage (%) 0-100 with 10 % major gridlines, x = Temperature (°C) 400-850 with 50 °C ticks. (a) is labelled Fe-13.5Mn-6.3Al-0.78C; (b) is labelled Fe-18Mn-7Al-0.85C; both are CALPHAD-type outputs (caption: FactSage 6.4). In (a) the α curve (α-ferrite, black) holds a plateau near 86-88 % from 400 °C to about 520 °C, then falls steeply, intersecting the rising γ-austenite curve near 630-640 °C at roughly 45 %; γ reaches 100 % at about 790 °C. Blue minor-phase curves in (a): M23C6 sits near 5 % and vanishes by ~550-560 °C; M7C3 appears only around 550-560 °C and vanishes near 680 °C; κ-carbide rises near 560 °C to a maximum of ~5 % around 620-650 °C and disappears near 740 °C. In (b), α starts near 85 % at 400 °C, falls with a shoulder around 550-600 °C, crosses γ near 610-620 °C (~45 %) and reaches 0 near 745 °C, where γ reaches 100 %; κ-carbide peaks at ~14 % near 500-520 °C and persists to ~720 °C, while M23C6 (~8 % at 400 °C) disappears near 500-510 °C. No numeric values are printed on the curves. The comparison shows the 18Mn alloy stabilises κ-carbide and destabilises M23C6 relative to the 13.5Mn alloy.

subfigures.description: Phase proportion (%) vs Temperature (°C, 400-850) for Fe-13.5Mn-6.3Al-0.78C. α-ferrite plateau ~86-88 % up to ~520 °C then drops to 0 near 790 °C; γ rises from near zero above ~540 °C to 100 % near 790 °C; minor phases M23C6 (~5 %, gone by ~550-560 °C), M7C3 (only ~550-680 °C) and κ-carbide (max ~5 % near 620-650 °C, gone ~740 °C).

Phase proportion (%) vs Temperature (°C, 400-850) for Fe-18Mn-7Al-0.85C. α decreases from ~85 % at 400 °C, with a shoulder near 550-600 °C, to 0 near 745 °C; γ reaches 100 % near 745 °C; κ-carbide shows a broad maximum ~14 % near 500-520 °C persisting to ~720 °C; M23C6 ~8 % at 400 °C disappears near 500-510 °C.

observations.observation: Both panels plot 'Phase percentage (%)' (0-100) against 'Temperature (°C)' (400-850) with no printed numeric data labels on the curves.
In (a), α keeps a plateau between roughly 86 and 88 % from 400 °C to about 520 °C before falling steeply to zero slightly below 800 °C.
In (a), γ-austenite stays near zero up to about 540 °C and reaches 100 % at about 790 °C, crossing the α curve at roughly 45 % near 630-640 °C.
In (a), M23C6 (blue) is present from 400 °C at about 5 % and disappears near 550-560 °C, while M7C3 appears only around 550-560 °C and vanishes near 680 °C.
In (a), κ-carbide (blue) appears near 560 °C, peaks at about 5 % around 620-650 °C and falls to zero near 740 °C.
In (b), α decreases from about 85 % at 400 °C, shows a shoulder between about 550 and 600 °C, and reaches zero near 745 °C where γ reaches 100 %.
In (b), κ-carbide rises from ~5 % at 400 °C to a broad maximum of about 14 % near 500-520 °C and persists until about 720 °C, far more stable than in (a).
In (b), M23C6 starts at about 8 % at 400 °C and disappears near 500-510 °C, earlier than in (a).
The caption states the panels give the calculated equilibrium phase proportions as a function of temperature for two alloys: (a) Fe-13.5Mn-6.3Al-0.78C [108] and (b) Fe-18Mn-7Al-0.85C [109].
The citing text states the phase proportions were calculated with FactSage 6.4 software.

The citing text states the samples were solution treated at 1100 °C for 1 h and then annealed for 100 h at temperatures from 500 to 875 °C, with the resulting phase constituents given in Table 3 (not part of this figure).
The two panels show the same phase set (γ, α, M23C6, M7C3/κ-carbide) but with shifted stability windows: M7C3 appears only in (a), and κ-carbide is much more stable in (b).

unreadable_items: Exact onset/offset temperatures of the minor phases (M23C6, M7C3, κ-carbide) can only be placed between the 50 °C gridlines; no printed values exist to confirm them.
Exact crossover temperature of the α and γ curves is not labelled in either panel.
